Fit the linear model with fixed provider effects

Source: R/model_linear_fe.R
fit_linear_fe.Rd

Fits \(Y_{ij} = \gamma_i + Z_{ij}^\top\beta + \epsilon_{ij}\) by least squares on the providers that pp_data() marked as included. The covariate coefficients come from the within-provider regression (every variable centred at its provider mean), so no provider dummy variables are formed; the provider effects are \(\hat\gamma_i = \bar Y_i - \bar Z_i^\top\hat\beta\).

Usage

fit_linear_fe(data)

Arguments

data

an object from pp_data() with a continuous (or any numeric) outcome.

Value

An object of class linear_fe:

coefficients

a list with gamma (provider effects, named by provider) and beta (covariate coefficients, named by covariate).

sigma

the residual standard deviation, \(\hat\sigma^2 = RSS / (n - m - p)\).

fitted, linear_predictor, residuals

per included row; linear_predictor is \(Z\hat\beta\).

loglik, aic, bic

Gaussian log-likelihood at the maximum-likelihood variance and the information criteria with \(m + p + 1\) parameters.

df_residual

\(n - m - p\).

vcov_beta

\(\hat\sigma^2 (\tilde Z^\top \tilde Z)^{-1}\) with \(\tilde Z\) the within-centred covariates.

data, vars, sizes, cutoff, rows

as in fit_logistic_fe().

See also

test.linear_fe(), summary.linear_fe(), standardize.linear_fe(), confint.linear_fe(), gamma_variance()

Examples

d <- sim_kecc(n_providers = 20, type = "continuous", seed = 1)
pd <- pp_data(d, y = "y", x = c("x1", "x2", "x3"), provider = "provider",
              patient = "patient", message = FALSE)
fit <- fit_linear_fe(pd)
fit
#> Linear model with fixed provider effects
#>   2679 rows, 20 providers, 3 covariates
#>   residual standard deviation 1.119 on 2656 degrees of freedom
#>   provider effects: median -0.06783, range -0.6820 to  0.8072
